# Impact analysis: current tariff (GLM-A-mono) to proposed tariff (GLM-B)

*Generated by `src/impact/dislocation.py` from `reports/tables/impact_*.csv`.*

The current tariff is GLM-A with BonusMalus 61-80 merged so that premium never falls as BonusMalus rises (GLM-A-mono, DECISIONS D041). An incumbent tariff whose no-claims scale reverses would not be realistic, and using it would mix that correction with the gains from the new interactions.

## Who moves

Both tariffs raise the same total premium (ratio 1.000000), so this is a redistribution. 34.7% of exposure moves by less than 5%; 11.3% moves by more than 20%.

| Change | Policies | Exposure | Mean change | Holdout observed / current | Holdout observed / proposed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| < -20% | 27,842 | 3.4% | -29.1% | 0.77 | 1.13 |
| -20% to -10% | 93,864 | 16.4% | -13.8% | 0.78 | 0.91 |
| -10% to -5% | 79,530 | 12.0% | -6.6% | 1.00 | 1.07 |
| -5% to +5% | 220,298 | 34.7% | -1.6% | 0.93 | 0.94 |
| +5% to +10% | 111,590 | 15.7% | +7.5% | 1.28 | 1.19 |
| +10% to +20% | 76,752 | 9.8% | +13.2% | 1.20 | 1.06 |
| > +20% | 68,115 | 7.9% | +26.1% | 1.15 | 0.89 |

Largest moves by factor level (at least 2,000 policy-years): VehBrand_grp B12 +7.2%; LogDensity_band 9.5+ +5.7%; Region_grp Ile-de-France +5.5%. Most affected segment: BonusMalus_band=100-110 & VehBrand_grp=B12 (-31.6%, 1,705 policy-years); top 10 in `impact_top_segments.csv`.

## Why: constraint versus interactions

| Step | Exposure moving > 5% | Moving > 20% | Mean absolute change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. GLM-A -> GLM-A-mono (BonusMalus constraint) | 8.5% | 0.0% | 1.7% |
| 2. GLM-A-mono -> GLM-B (interactions) | 65.3% | 11.3% | 9.6% |
| total: GLM-A -> GLM-B | 67.7% | 12.4% | 10.1% |

The BonusMalus constraint moves 8.5% of exposure by more than 5%; the three BonusMalus interactions (by driver age, for brand B12, and for a group of mainly urban and southern regions) move 65.3%. The proposal analysed here is the second step.

## Is it supported by experience

Observed loss cost on the holdout, which neither tariff was fitted on, is capped claims plus the flat large-loss load (all-claims ratios are in the table file). The proposed premium is closer to experience than the current one in 6 of 7 bands; not in -10% to -5%. For the largest decreases the ratio moves from 0.77 against current and 1.13 against proposed; for the largest increases, 1.15 against current and 0.89 against proposed. Band ratios carry sampling error of roughly +/-5% to +/-13% (95%).

## Capping trade-off

A +/-15% cap on year-one change, not re-balanced, changes revenue by -0.3%. Re-balanced (scale 1.0039 before capping), it delivers 78.6% of the intended movement and keeps 105.1% of the holdout Gini improvement; 17.1% of exposure sits at the cap. Holdout Gini is noisy, so this indicates rather than proves the value of a cap.

## Before implementation

- Retention and elasticity: the analysis is static; large increases may lapse and change the mix. No demand data.
- Competitor position: large decreases may already be below market; large increases may not be achievable.
- Regulatory and fairness review: region and density can proxy protected characteristics; the age interaction moves young and older drivers. No fairness testing was done.
- BonusMalus drives every change and is itself a record of claims (LIMITATIONS).
- A multi-year transition for policies at the cap.
